kurz: Why repaying debt is a form of investment, how the interest rate determines how dangerous a debt is, and how much the order of repayment matters.

bloecke.md:
A loan is an investment with the sign reversed. An instalment loan at 6.2% is a position that costs 6.2% every year with certainty. It sits on the debt side of your wealth and so does not appear in any portfolio overview. Repaying it is therefore not a sacrifice. With every repayment you acquire a guaranteed, tax-free return equal to the loan's interest rate.

Overall, the situation in Germany is less strained than the advertising suggests. In 2023, households had on average around €35,300 of debt on their books, of which about €30,800 was mortgages and only around €2,200 consumer debt. Debt in Germany is therefore mainly property debt. The problem is the distribution, which the average conceals. Households with consumer debt usually have several such debts, and they are almost always expensive.

bloecke.unter: How dangerous a debt is depends on the combination of interest rate and lasting value received, not on its size.

felder.text: Mortgage loan secured by a land charge, interest-free state loan during education. The debt finances something that is still there after the last instalment.
Loan for a qualification or business equipment. It is justified solely by the return it makes possible. This return has to be estimated in advance.
Interest-free instalment plan, family loan. The danger here is getting used to a monthly budget that is permanently committed in advance.
Arranged overdraft, unarranged overdraft, revolving credit card balances, spirals of reminders and debt collection. The debt grows faster than the capacity to repay it increases.

bloecke.md:
## Three test questions for loans

The **interest question** checks whether the annual percentage rate (APR) is higher than the return that can be achieved with certainty after tax. In that case, repaying is unreservedly the better investment, because the saving is certain and the return is not.

The **substance question** checks whether something remains after the last instalment that has value or generates income. A flat or an education remains; a holiday does not.

The **resilience question** checks whether the instalment could still be paid for three months without full income and without taking out another loan. This test is the most important one and the one carried out least often. It determines whether a sustainable debt stays sustainable.

bloecke.md:
The borrowing rate (Sollzins) is the price of the money; the price of the entire contract is stated as the [[annual percentage rate (APR)]]. Under the Price Indication Ordinance (Preisangabenverordnung), it includes all term-dependent costs and the timing of every single payment. Only the APR allows two offers to be compared. The Federal Court of Justice (BGH) has declared processing fees in consumer loan agreements invalid. Since then, banks have been generating this income through other items.

The most important of these items is [[payment protection insurance]]. If taking it out is a condition of the loan, its costs must be included in the APR. If it is formally voluntary, this does not apply. That is why it is sold as voluntary, even though it can make the loan noticeably more expensive. Since an amendment to the Insurance Contract Act, for general consumer loans it may only be taken out at least one week after the loan agreement (Section 7a(5) VVG). This rule was introduced because the insurance used to be sold along with the loan when the contract was signed.

bloecke.erklaerung: Annuity payment of an instalment loan. The monthly interest rate is calculated from the APR using i = (1 + p)^(1/12) − 1, not by dividing p by twelve.
bloecke.beispiel: With €10,000, 6.2% APR and 48 months, the result is i = 0.5025%, an instalment of €234.99 and total payments of €11,280, of which €1,280 is interest.

bloecke.md:
The starting point is €10,000 permanently in the overdraft at 11.5%. If only the interest is paid out of salary, this costs €1,150 a year, and after ten years the debt still stands at €10,000.

With option 1, the debt stays in the overdraft and is repaid at €235 a month. This takes 55 months and costs around €2,711 in interest.

With option 2, the debt is refinanced with an instalment loan at 6.2% APR over a term of 48 months. The instalment is also around €235, and the interest comes to €1,280.

Simply switching the contract therefore saves around €1,430 and seven months, with no additional sacrifice. The condition, however, is that the overdraft limit is reduced afterwards. Otherwise, after a short time, both debts exist side by side.

bloecke.md:
With **buy now, pay later**, payment is deferred. The deferral is free as long as the deadline is met. Costs only arise on late payment, namely through reminder fees, default interest (capped for consumers at five percentage points above the basic rate of interest (Basiszinssatz), Section 288 BGB, the Civil Code) and finally through debt collection. Because each purchase is a separate contract, it is easy to lose track of the total while each individual instalment remains manageable.

Revolving repayment is often the default setting on credit cards. The interest rate is in double digits, and the minimum payment is set so that the debt hardly falls if the card continues to be used. The card provider earns money from the interest. BNPL providers, by contrast, earn mainly from a fee that the merchant pays for each purchase, because the merchant expects more and larger purchases as a result. That is why the deferral is made so convenient with both products.

## The avalanche and snowball methods

With several debts, you have to decide in which order to repay them. The [[avalanche method]] covers all minimum payments and puts every additional free euro towards the debt with the highest interest rate. It is mathematically optimal. The [[snowball method]] first repays the smallest debt regardless of the interest rate and then directs the freed-up instalment to the next one. It is mathematically worse but psychologically more powerful, because the first visible success comes sooner.

An illustrative calculation shows how large the difference is. It uses €2,400 of overdraft at 11.5%, a €6,000 instalment loan at 6.2% with a €150 minimum payment and €600 of interest-free instalment payments at €50 a month. A total of €500 a month is available. As in the formula above, the monthly interest rates are derived from the APRs.

bloecke.unter: The avalanche and snowball curves almost overlap; the gap to the minimum-payments variant is many times larger.

serien.name: minimum payments only, overdraft stays in place

bloecke.md: The avalanche takes 19 months and costs around €486 in interest; the snowball takes 20 months and costs around €515. The difference is therefore around €29 and one month. In return, with the snowball the first debt is paid off after 2 months instead of 9. If, on the other hand, only the minimum payments are made and the overdraft stays in place, the outstanding debt after 24 months is still around €5,935. The choice of method is therefore worth a few tens of euros, whereas the pace of repayment is worth thousands.

## Repay or invest

The comparison between repaying and investing is usually made with gross figures, and then it is wrong. Capital income is subject to flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% plus a solidarity surcharge of 5.5% on it, 26.375% in total, plus church tax where applicable. An interest payment saved, by contrast, is tax-free and certain.

For an investment to beat an instalment loan at 6.2%, it must earn around 8.4% before tax. To beat an overdraft at 11.5%, around 15.6% is needed, and reliably so, not just as a long-term average. Such returns do not exist without considerable risk. One qualification applies as long as the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 has not been used up. Up to this amount the income remains tax-free, and the hurdle falls to the loan interest rate itself.

There are three exceptions to the “repay first” rule:

1. The emergency fund takes priority over special repayments. Without a reserve, the next car repair leads straight back into the overdraft, and the progress made so far is lost.
2. Some payments only flow if you invest, for example the employer's contribution to capital-forming payments (vermögenswirksame Leistungen) or to an occupational pension (betriebliche Altersvorsorge). This money yields an immediate return that no consumer loan rate can match.
3. An old mortgage loan with a very low interest rate and a long fixed-rate period does not have to be repaid as a priority. What matters here is the fixed-rate period, special repayment rights and the early repayment charge, not the rule of thumb.

bloecke.unter: Shares of the cases recorded by debt counselling services; the figures do not add up to 100% because other and unknown triggers are not shown.

bloecke.md: The two most common triggers are illness and unemployment, which together account for around 35% of cases. Poor household management, widely thought to be the main cause, lies well behind at 11.7%. This changes nothing about the arithmetic of interest, but it does change how the problem should be understood. In most cases, over-indebtedness is an event risk rather than a character problem. It therefore cannot be solved with discipline either; it requires advice.

Lower the overdraft limit to the amount needed, switch off the credit card's revolving repayment function and delete BNPL accounts. Without this step, the debts you have paid off soon build up again.

bloecke.md: Over-indebtedness exists when seizable income, after deducting essential living costs, is permanently no longer enough to service the liabilities. Typical signs are loans taken out to service other loans, court payment orders (Mahnbescheide) and garnishment of the account. At that point no repayment strategy will help any more, but a recognised debt counselling service will. Such services are offered by consumer advice centres (Verbraucherzentralen), the charities Caritas and Diakonie, and local authority offices, free of charge or for an income-related fee. They negotiate out-of-court settlements and prepare consumer insolvency proceedings (Verbraucherinsolvenz), which end after three years with the discharge of residual debt (Restschuldbefreiung). Following case law of the European Court of Justice, SCHUFA (German credit reference agency) now stores this discharge for only six months. Two steps make sense immediately: having your current account run as a garnishment-protected account (Pfändungsschutzkonto) and rejecting any offer that promises “refinancing without SCHUFA” in return for payment in advance.

- Consumer loan agreements can be withdrawn from within 14 days. The period only begins once all mandatory information has been provided in full.
- Instalment loans and other general consumer loans can be repaid early at any time (Section 500 BGB). The [[early repayment charge]] is limited to 1% of the amount repaid early, or 0.5% if the remaining term is one year or less. It may never exceed the interest for the remaining term (Section 502 BGB). Mortgage loans with a fixed-rate period, by contrast, can only be repaid early if there is a legitimate interest, such as selling the property, and the charge has no percentage cap.
- Customers who overdraw their account substantially over a longer period are entitled to an offer of advice from the bank (Section 504a BGB).
- Default interest charged to consumers is capped at five percentage points above the basic rate of interest (Section 288 BGB). Reminder fees must correspond to the costs actually incurred.
- According to case law of the Federal Court of Justice, processing fees in consumer loan agreements are invalid. Fees paid without legal grounds could be reclaimed.

mitnehmen: A loan is an investment with the sign reversed, so every repayment earns a certain, tax-free return equal to the APR.
Only the APR allows offers to be compared, and whether refinancing is worthwhile is shown solely by the total interest cost over the term, not by a lower monthly instalment.
The avalanche and snowball methods are usually only a few tens of euros apart, whereas consistent repayment and paying only the minimum are years apart.
To beat an overdraft at 11.5%, an investment would have to earn around 15.6% before tax with certainty, and no such investment exists.
Over-indebtedness most often results from illness or unemployment, and often from separation too; in this situation, debt counselling is the right way forward, not a repayment method.

begriffe.text: The price of a loan including all term-dependent costs and the timing of payments, calculated under the Price Indication Ordinance (Preisangabenverordnung). It is the only figure that allows loan offers to be compared. The borrowing rate (Sollzins) is not suitable for this.
A repayment order in which, once all minimum payments have been made, every free euro goes to the debt with the highest interest rate. It is mathematically optimal.
A repayment order in which the smallest debt is repaid first, regardless of the interest rate. It costs slightly more interest but brings the first visible success sooner.

Insurance that covers loan instalments in the event of death, incapacity for work or unemployment. It is only included in the APR if taking it out is compulsory. For general consumer loans such as instalment loans, it may only be taken out at least one week after the loan agreement has been concluded.

A fee for repaying a loan early. For general consumer loans such as instalment loans, the charge is limited to 1% of the amount repaid (0.5% if the remaining term is one year or less) and never exceeds the interest for the remaining term. This limit does not apply to mortgage loans.
